title: A guarantee fare guarantees a category.
subtitle: Not a cabin, not a deck, not a side, and certainly not the quiet one.

text: You have bought a category and handed over the choice.
sub: The line assigns you whatever is left when the people who chose have finished choosing. What is left is, by definition, what nobody wanted.

right.label: Chosen
items: Known from the day you book

items.head: Pick two of four
items.body: Credit, drinks, wifi, gratuities — bundled to make categories look interchangeable. They are not.

items.head: The upgrade that isn't
items.body: An offer to move you up a category can move you to a worse position on a higher deck.

items.head: The bid-to-upgrade email
items.body: A bid wins you a category and no control at all. Read what it does to your booked cabin first.

points.label: A near-full ship
points.value: Little is left in any case. The saving is real and the risk is small.

points.label: Short, sheltered
points.value: Three nights in sheltered water forgives almost any position on the plan.

points.label: Deep off-season fares
points.value: When the gap is large enough, take the money and accept the lottery.

points.label: Longer than a week
points.value: Never. You will live with that position for too many nights.

text: Pay the assignment fee. It is the cheapest thing on the invoice.
sub: Choosing rather than being assigned costs a modest amount per person, and it is the only line on a cruise invoice that protects every single night of the voyage.

title: Send this to anyone holding a guarantee fare.
body: Or tell me the category you've been offered and I'll tell you what the worst cabin in it looks like — because that is the one you may be given.
